title: Awami League and Chhatra League supporters clash with police in Gopalganj
seoTitle: Gopalganj protests by Awami League supporters

tea.why: Supporters of the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina are protesting to demand her return to Bangladesh from exile.
tea.want: The return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to Bangladesh.
tea.changed: Nov 10: Authorities deployed six platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to restore order following clashes and arson.

summary: On November 10, 2026, supporters of the banned Awami League and its student wing, the Chhatra League, held protests in Gopalganj, Bangladesh. Demonstrators blocked roads in Tungipara, Kashiani, and Sadar upazilas, setting fires to tires and wood to disrupt traffic. Clashes occurred between protesters and police, who used tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse the crowds. During the unrest, a police vehicle was set on fire, and several shops were vandalized. Local authorities reported that at least 10 people were injured, and eight individuals were arrested. By the afternoon, the district administration stated that the situation was under control, with six platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) deployed to maintain security. The protests were part of a wider series of demonstrations by pro-Hasina activists across the country.
demands: Return of Sheikh Hasina to Bangladesh
response: Police used tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse protesters. The government deployed six platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to the district to maintain order. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that instability caused by external influence would not be tolerated.

updates.text: Protesters blocked roads and clashed with police in Tungipara, setting a police vehicle on fire.
Authorities deployed six platoons of BGB to Gopalganj to restore order.
Police confirmed the situation was under control by the afternoon and traffic resumed on the Dhaka-Khulna highway.
